Issued at 1152 PM CDT Sat Aug 8 2026

This Morning - Early Afternoon: Storms Likely, Some Strong to Severe

Initial forecast concerns this morning will feature likely storm 
development as a 700mb shortwave moves through the Dakotas and into 
the Upper Mississippi Valley. As this occurs, increasing warm air 
advection and instability aloft will allow for a profound 
instability gradient to setup across portions of the region. The 
overall evolution manifests as discrete convection develops 
west of the local area and progresses eastward during the 
overnight and early morning hours. As this occurs, cold pools 
with widespread discrete convection associated with the wave 
will likely result in upscale growth with much of the CAMs 
agreeing on pushing an MCS/MCV through the region with some 
differences on exact timing but generally during the mid-morning
hours. 

Overall, the main question during this period will be exactly 
how much storms maintain as they move through the local area 
since they will be pushing into a lower instability environment,
especially near the Mississippi River. The primary threat with 
these storms would be damaging winds with the organized cold 
pools and favorably oriented 0-3km shear vector. If a more 
coherent MCV with embedded bowing structures can manifest (as 
shown in the very recent 09.02z HRRR and 09.00z RRFS), would not
be shocked to see some gusts approaching 70 mph. An embedded 
tornado cannot be fully ruled out with this given the 
aforementioned 0-3km shear vector, however fairly respectable 
capping present over the region would make this fairly unlikely.
This complex would generally be progressive in nature with much
of the CAMs generally having it exiting east of the local area 
by early afternoon. 

This Evening - Overnight: Slight Chance for Redeveloping Storms 

Additional storm development later into the evening will heavily 
hinge on how quickly convection during the morning and early 
afternoon pushes through the region. Based on the current state of 
the CAMs, convection later into the evening would seem less 
favorable as the cold pool from this MCS would likely push the 
instability gradient further south of the area. This being 
said, if we can recover instability quick enough and convect by 
evening, the environment would favor some multi-cellular 
clusters with embedded supercells. In this scenario, large hail,
damaging wind gusts and locally heavy rainfall would be the 
primary threats with continued development along the instability
gradient. Again, need to emphasize though that this is heavily 
contingent on if we can recover any instability back into the 
region in light of the morning and early afternoon convection. 

Monday - Wednesday: Additional Storm Chances, Severe Storms and 
Locally Heavy Rainfall Possible

As we head into the start of the work week, persistent zonal to 
northwesterly flow will allow occasional shortwave 
perturbations to move through the region. Consequently, 
expecting additional chances for showers and storms. However, 
much of this will be contingent on how storms for previous days 
modify the instability gradient which will be the primary focus 
for where storms form. Deterministic guidance (GFS/NAM/EC) 
generally wants to highlight an additional shortwave 
perturbation that moves through the region later Monday evening 
and into the overnight. With fairly steep mid-level lapse rates
and some stronger flow aloft, wouldn't be surprised if initial 
development could trend supercellular before organizing cold 
pools would trend towards a damaging wind threat. The trouble 
with this again is where storms form will be contingent on where
the instability gradient is during this timeframe, which could
very likely remain south of the local area.

Heading into Tuesday and Wednesday, the aforementioned zonal to 
northwesterly flow will persist over the local area. Consequently, 
shower and storm chances (15-30% in the recent NBM) will remain 
across the local area, however exact details at this point remain 
largely uncertain due to evolution of how earlier days storms may 
manifest. In any case, will need to watch for if repeated rounds of 
storms may track over the same locations through mid-week as 
precipitable waters remaining around 1.5-2" and deep warm cloud 
depths would suggest storms from today through mid-week will likely 
be efficient rainfall producers. Consequently, flooding concerns 
would increase if multiple rounds of storms occur over the same 
locations through mid-week.
